_readme: Living taxonomy, not a fixed enum. classify.py prefers matching an existing category via its keywords; add new categories here (with a keyword list) if a cluster of papers doesn't fit any existing one well and is large enough to deserve its own bucket -- rerun classify.py (via merge_corpus.py) after editing. 'uncategorized' is not a real category, it's what unmatched papers get until the taxonomy is extended to cover them. Prefer specific multi-word phrases over generic bare words as keywords: score_category() counts raw occurrences per keyword with no length weighting, so a common bare word (e.g. 'tracking', 'benchmark', 'planning') tends to win purely on frequency even in papers where that's not really the topic, crowding out the category that's actually the best fit -- confirmed on real data (see DECISIONS.md).
